symptom: `alter page … { set (DateFormat: Custom, CustomDateFormat: 'dd/MM/yyyy') on dp }` on a picker whose stored format is not Custom: check refused it ("`DateFormat: Custom` needs a pattern … in the same statement") in either order and as two SETs, so exec's pre-check refused it too; --no-check wrote it and mx check passed (mendixlabs/mxcli#1743)
cause: setWidgetFormattingMut refused Custom on the STORED blank pattern, relying on exec applying properties in name order; check's checkSetOp dry-runs one property at a time on a fresh probe of the stored widget, where Custom never sees the pattern. The whole-statement post-check (checkDateFormatAfterSet, #977) ran only in exec
file: mdl/backend/pagemutator/mutator.go (in-setter guard removed), mdl/executor/validate_alter_set.go (checkDateFormatSet: earlier SETs on the widget, then this one whole, then the #977 check); test alter_set_date_format_pedapp_test.go
insight: A rule between two properties cannot live in a per-property setter: whichever setter runs first sees half the statement, and a per-property dry run sees less. Put the cross-property rule after the whole statement, and give check the SAME judgement on a probe carrying the statement's earlier SETs — exec applies them in sequence on one copy, check probes the stored widget per SET. assertAgree (check then exec, same verdict) is the test shape for every check/exec disagreement. Control: before the change the three reported forms fail assertAgree; Custom with no pattern is refused by both throughout.
